subject: MSA intake — Brightleaf AI: initial docs and redline priority
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA intake: Brightleaf AI — initial docs & ask

Hi Stephanie — attaching Brightleaf's initial MSA and draft order form (see attachments). Quick context: Brightleaf (AI infrastructure for content generation) is looking to move from pilot to paid in Q4; AE asked for standard Redwood MSA but customer sent their version with a few commercial tweaks.

Can Legal please:
- Prioritize review of sections: Data use & retention, IP (derivative/feedback), Indemnity, Limitation of Liability (cap + exclusions), Termination for convenience, and Exhibit A (scope/billing).
- Produce a tracked-changes redline (Word) and a 1-page risk summary highlighting any clauses we should escalate to leadership.

Customer asks/flags from initial read:
- Liability cap tied to 24 months' fees
- Wants indemnity narrower on Redwood claims
- Wants no audit rights for subprocessors

Timeline: Customer is asking for our redline by COB Oct 16 (they have an internal procurement window). HubSpot deal id DEAL-3472.

Attachments: Brightleaf_MSA_v0.9_redline.docx, Brightleaf_OrderForm_Draft.pdf

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: Re: MSA intake: Brightleaf AI — initial docs & ask

Karthik — thanks for the packet.

I will queue this as High for Legal intake. A few quick asks to help prioritize our redline:
- Do we have the expected initial ARR/first-year spend for the cap conversation? (even a range is fine)
- Does the customer expect any data residency constraints (they're US-headquartered but mentioned EU customers)?

Marissa / Kimberly — please call out the top 3 items we should push back on vs. accept. If you can, include a short suggested fallback for sales to offer (e.g., 12 months' fees cap, mutual indemnity language, limited audit on subprocessors with notice).

I'll block a 30-min sync for 11:30 PT if you think cross-team discussion is helpful — otherwise please post the redline and summary in Drive and ping me.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Contracts Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA intake: Brightleaf AI — initial docs & ask

Thanks — reviewed the attachments. I put together an initial pass and a short risk memo (attached). High-level summary up front:

1) Liability cap: Customer proposes 24 months' fees. Sales will want to avoid a hard no; suggested approach: counter with 12 months' fees (or $X min) and keep carve-outs for wilful misconduct and breaches of confidentiality. If this is strategic (net new logo, >$500k ARR year 1) we can bring to leadership for exception.

2) Indemnity: Customer's draft is one-sided. Propose mutual indemnity for third-party IP claims, with Redwood indemnifying for our products/services only. Do not accept broad carrier or downstream indemnities.

3) Data / Subprocessors / Audit: Brightleaf removed our audit right for subprocessors and limited data transfer language. Ask: Do they have SOC2 + a list of subprocessors? If not, we should retain a limited audit right (notice + remediation window) and require contractual flow-down to subprocessors. Also propose standard data retention language and a 90-day deletion window after termination unless a regulatory hold applies.

4) Termination & Transition: Customer included a short termination-for-convenience clause with 30 days' notice — ask Sales whether they need this now or can accept 90 days' notice. Also ensure export of data obligations are explicit in Exhibit B.

5) Exhibit A (Services/scope): Their Order Form is missing clear billing cadence and PO information. Need sales to confirm whether billing will be monthly vs. annual prepay and whether they require a PO. That impacts invoicing and the cap language (if annual prepay, cap calculation differs).

Attachments included: Redlines_Brightleaf_MSA_v1.docx (tracked changes), Redline_Summary.docx (1-page memo).

Questions for Sales (Karthik):
- Confirm expected first-year ARR / contract value range.
- Confirm billing cadence (monthly vs. annual) and whether they will issue a PO.
- Any regulatory data residency commitments we must accept?

If we can get answers today, I can finalize the redline by EOB tomorrow (Oct 13). Otherwise target internal sign-off by Oct 15 to hit customer deadline.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Marissa. I can confirm initial ARR expectation is in the $150k–$250k range year one (we're still finalizing order). Billing: customer prefers annual invoicing but will accept quarterly. They said PO is likely but not guaranteed. No explicit EU residency requirements on the initial deal, but they serve some EU customers and will ask about data transfers — I will loop in Elena and Tom to get clarity.

I'll coordinate with the customer on the two billing questions and push for a SOC2 report from their security contact. Targeting internal final by Oct 15 as discussed.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Mid-Market
Redwood Inference
